CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Susan Jakubowski, Mayor  www.cityofsanmarino.org
Steve Talt, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone
Steven W. Huang, DDS, Council Member  (626) 300-0709 Fax
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber
Ken Ude, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Marcella Marlowe, Ph.D., City Manager  San Marino, CA 91108

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 11, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.
  SAN MARINO CENTER
  1800 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council with
valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically, adjourned
meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact
the City Clerk via email at cityclerk@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-0705 prior
to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the City Council may teleconference into the meeting without noticing each
teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
To protect both staff, our constituents, and elected officials, it is recommended that members of
the public wear a mask indoors, per the State and County Health Department’s current Health
Officer Orders. Given the seriousness of COVID-19, you are encouraged to provide input
electronically if you do not feel comfortable attending in person.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – MAY 11, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 6

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  1) Via Computer for Video Streaming:
  Website: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89531199903
  Meeting ID: 895 3119 9903
  2) Via Phone for Audio Only:
  Phone Number: (669) 900-9128
  Meeting ID: 895 3119 9903

How to offer public comment from home:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to cityclerk@cityofsanmarino.org until 3:00
  p.m. the day of the meeting, to be read by the City Clerk during public comment. Lengthy
  public comment may be summarized in the interest of time. Any comments received after
  3:00 p.m. will be included in the public comment record but will not be read at the
  meeting.
  2) Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
  during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Council Member Huang, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Council
  Member Ude, Vice Mayor Talt, and Mayor Jakubowski

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200
Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman Building,
1560 Pasqualito Drive.  The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant to
state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting agenda
(Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on duration
of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – MAY 11, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 6

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to read
the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First Reading must
be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require having the title read.
However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or resolution be read in its entirety
before taking any action.

  PRESENTATION

1. PRESENTATION OF A PROCLAMATION IN RECOGNITION OF MAY BEING
  ASIAN AMERICAN PACIFIC ISLANDER HERITAGE MONTH

2. INTRODUCTION OF THE DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION TASK
  FORCE MEMBERS

3. PRESENTATION OF A PROCLAMATION IN RECOGNITION OF MAY BEING
  HISTORIC PRESERVATION MONTH

4. UPDATES ON WATER RESTRICTIONS

  NEW BUSINESS

5. APPROVAL OF THE SPRING 2022 PUBLIC TREE REMOVAL LIST
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Spring 2022
  recommended tree removal list and authorize the Director of Parks and Public Works to
  move forward to properly remove the trees on the list.

6. AWARD  OF  A  CONSTRUCTION  AGREEMENT  FOR  STREET
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM PROJECT NO. 21-9271 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $3,532,222 TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT, INCLUDING APPROVAL OF A 5%
  CONTRACT CONTINGENCY; AWARD OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT FOR CONSTRUCTION INSPECTION SERVICES FOR THE
  STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM PROJECT NO. 21-9271 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $79,934 TO Z&K CONSULTANTS
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council (1) approve the plans and
  specifications for the Street Rehabilitation Program Project No. 21-9271; (2) find that the
  Street Rehabilitation Program Project No. 21-9271 is categorically exempt under Sections
  15301(c) and 15302 of the California Environmental Quality Act and direct the Director of
  Community Development to file the notice of exemption with the state and County of Los
  Angeles; (3) award a construction agreement to All American Asphalt for the Street
  Rehabilitation Program Project No. 21-9271 in a total amount not-to-exceed $3,532,222; (4)
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – MAY 11, 2022  PAGE 4 OF 6

  award a professional services agreement in the amount of $79,934 to Z&K Consultants for
  professional construction inspection services; and (5) authorize the Parks and Public Works
  Director to approve contract change orders and other contingencies in a cumulative amount
  not-to-exceed $353,222.

7. APPROVAL OF ORDINANCE NO. O-22-1390 (FIRST READING)
  IMPLEMENTING ASSEMBLY BILL 481 AND APPROVING A POLICY FOR THE
  USE OF MILITARY EQUIPMENT BY THE SAN MARINO POLICE
  DEPARTMENT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and introduce
  for first reading by title only, Ordinance No. O-22-1390 an Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of San Marino, Implementing AB 481 and Approving a Policy for the Use of Military
  Equipment by the SMPD.

8. APPROVAL OF ORDINANCE NO. O-22-1392 (FIRST READING) AMENDING
  THE CITY CODE TO MAKE UPDATES TO THE RECREATION COMMISSION
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and introduce
  for first reading by title only, Ordinance No. O-22-1392 an Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of San Marino Amending the City Code Making Updates to the Recreation
  Commission.

9. APPROVAL OF ORDINANCE NO. O-22-1391 (FIRST READING) AMENDING
  THE CITY CODE TO UPDATE THE ORDER OF SUCCESSION FOR THE
  DIRECTOR OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and introduce
  for first reading by title only, Ordinance No. O-22-1391 an Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of San Marino Amending the City Code to Update the Order of Succession for the
  Director of Emergency Services.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

10. RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR APRIL
  2022

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of April 2022.

11. RECEIVE AND FILE CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR MARCH 2022

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for the month of March 2022.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – MAY 11, 2022  PAGE 5 OF 6

12. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the special meeting of
  April 13, 2022, the regular meeting of April 13, 2022, the special meeting of April 22, 2022,
  and the adjourned regular meeting of April 29, 2022.

13. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-22-21 TO CONTINUE HYBRID PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO AB 361

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. R-22-21 re-
  authorizing the City Council and the City’s Boards and Commissions to continue
  teleconference accessibility for conducting public meetings pursuant to AB 361.

14. UPDATE ON CITY RESPONSE TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the May 11, 2022
  report on the City’s response to the COVID-19 Pandemic.

15. AWARD OF A MULTI-YEAR CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT WITH CJ
  CONCRETE CONSTRUCTION, INC. FOR THE MULTI-YEAR SIDEWALK
  REPLACEMENT PROGRAM WITH THE FY 2022-23 (YEAR 1) CONTRACT
  AMOUNT OF $418,300, INCLUDING APPROVAL OF A 5% CONTRACT
  CONTINGENCY AND A TOTAL ESTIMATED CONTRACT VALUE OF
  $3,405,805
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council award the multi-year sidewalk
  replacement program agreement to CJ Concrete Construction Inc with the fiscal year 2022-
  23 (Year 1) contract amount of $418,300 with a 5 percent construction contingency,
  contingent on the adoption of the FY 2022-23 budget, and with subsequent contract fiscal
  years contingent on an appropriation by the City Council, with the City Manager being
  authorized to execute the agreement on behalf of the City, as well as two one-year contract
  extensions subject to City Council appropriation and satisfactory performance.

16. APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH DYNAMIC BUILDING MAINTENANCE THROUGH APRIL 30, 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the professional
  maintenance service agreement with Dynamic Building Maintenance through April 30, 2023,
  for their professional janitorial services in City facilities, and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement on behalf of the City.

17. APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R-22-19, ADOPTING A LIST OF STREET
  PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 FUNDED BY SB 1, THE ROAD REPAIR
  AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. R-22-19
  adopting a list of Fiscal Year 2022-23 projects to be funded by SB 1 Road Maintenance and
  Rehabilitation Account Funds.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – MAY 11, 2022  PAGE 6 OF 6

18. APPROVAL OF A REQUEST TO WAIVE THE SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT FEES
  FOR 4TH OF JULY COMMUNITY PARTNER EVENTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council waive the Special Event Permit
  fees associated with the 4th of July Pavilion, 4th of July Parade, and the JP Blecksmith Run.

19. APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION TO ESTABLISH FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 PUBLIC
  SAFETY SPECIAL TAX LEVY

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. R-22-15
  establishing the Public Safety Special Tax Levy for Fiscal Year 2022-23.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City received
by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at
least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at
the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108,
and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will available for review at the City
Council meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

ADJOURNMENT

Dated: May 6, 2022  CHRISTINA BAKER
Posted: May 6, 2022  CITY CLERK
